assets.content:
---
id: go-goroutine-without-context
language: go
severity: warning
message: Goroutine started without passing context. Pass a context.Context parameter to support cancellation propagation.
note: A goroutine without context can keep running after its parent function
  returns, leaking goroutines at service shutdown.
rule:
  pattern: "go func() {\n  $$$BODY\n}()\n"
---
id: go-defer-in-loop
language: go
# warning, not error: this is a resource-hygiene rule, not a security rule. The
# pre-write scan gate translates error severity directly into a refused write,
# which is too strong for a pattern that is often deliberate. The rule keeps
# reporting on the warning path.
severity: warning
message: defer inside a loop holds the file/resource open until the loop's enclosing function returns.
note: defer inside a loop does not run until the function returns. Extract the
  loop body into a separate function or close explicitly.
# Expressed structurally (a defer statement nested inside a for statement)
# rather than as an indented multi-line pattern: the literal block form matched
# nothing under ast-grep 0.40.x, while this form fires on any loop-carried
# defer and stays silent outside loops.
rule:
  all:
    - kind: defer_statement
    - inside:
        stopBy: end
        kind: for_statement
---
id: go-channel-send-no-select
language: go
severity: warning
message: Channel send without select-default. The goroutine can block forever if no receiver is ready.
note: 'Use the select { case ch <- v: default: } pattern, or select together
  with context.Done().'
rule:
  pattern: $CHAN <- $VALUE

---
id: go-error-ignored-blank
language: go
# warning, not error: this is a style rule, not a security rule. The pre-write
# scan gate translates error severity directly into a refused write, and
# `_ = foo()` is a routine Go idiom, so error severity here would refuse
# ordinary edits across a codebase. The rule keeps reporting on the warning
# path.
severity: warning
message: The returned error is discarded with _. Handle it or mark the intentional ignore with a comment.
note: Ignoring an error can cause data corruption or silent failures. At
  minimum, log the error or add a // nolint:errcheck comment.
rule:
  pattern: $_, $ERR = $FUNC($$$ARGS)
---
id: go-error-not-wrapped
language: go
severity: warning
message: 'Error returned as-is without context. Use the fmt.Errorf("operation: %w", err) pattern.'
note: Error wrapping is essential for tracing the error path without a stack
  trace. The %w verb is required for errors.Is/As to work correctly.
# The bare `return $ERR` pattern matched every single-expression return
# (return nil/0/true/""/f()), producing ~16k false positives and a
# catastrophic autofix that wrapped non-error returns in fmt.Errorf. The
# name constraint ($ERR regex ^err(e?|s)$) is the type proxy: Go variables
# named err/errs are overwhelmingly errors. The fix fires under the SAME
# guard as the match, so non-matches are never rewritten.
rule:
  pattern: return $ERR
fix: 'return fmt.Errorf("TODO: operation: %w", $ERR)'
constraints:
  ERR:
    regex: '^err(e?|s)$'
---
id: go-errors-new-in-var
language: go
severity: warning
message: errors.New() assigned to a package-level variable — the sentinel error pattern. Mind backward compatibility.
note: Exporting a sentinel error as a variable makes it part of the package
  API. Changing it later is a breaking change for callers.
rule:
  pattern: var $NAME = errors.New("$MSG")

# Go hardcoding-detection rules.
#
# These rules detect common hardcoding anti-patterns in Go source code.
# Severity levels:
#   - error: intended to block a commit in a quality gate
#   - warning: intended to be reported without blocking
---
id: go-no-hardcoded-api-url
language: go
severity: warning
message: "Extract the API URL to a package-level constant or configuration value. Hardcoded URLs reduce maintainability and make environment changes error-prone."
note: "A literal API endpoint embedded in source cannot be changed per environment without a recompile. Move it to a constant, an environment variable, or a configuration file."
rule:
  kind: interpreted_string_literal
  regex: '^"https://api\.'
---
id: go-no-duplicate-coverage-threshold
language: go
severity: warning
message: "Use a shared coverage-threshold constant instead of redefining the value locally. A single source of truth prevents drift across packages."
note: "Duplicating a numeric quality threshold in more than one place lets the copies drift apart. Define it once and reference it."
rule:
  pattern: const $NAME = 85.0

---
id: go-interface-empty-not-any
language: go
severity: warning
message: Uses interface{}. Prefer any (Go 1.18+).
note: any is a type alias of interface{} and reads better. It is the recommended
  spelling on Go 1.18 and later.
rule:
  pattern: interface{}
fix: any
---
id: go-time-since-manual
language: go
severity: warning
message: Use time.Since(t) instead of time.Now().Sub(t).
note: time.Since(t) is identical to time.Now().Sub(t) but more readable.
rule:
  pattern: time.Now().Sub($T)
fix: time.Since($T)
---
id: go-bytes-buffer-string-conversion
language: go
severity: warning
message: 'Possible unnecessary allocation in []byte/string conversion. Consider strings.Builder.'
note: string([]byte{...}) always performs a fresh allocation. For repeated
  concatenation, strings.Builder is more efficient.
rule:
  pattern: string([]byte{$$$ITEMS})

---
id: go-map-no-ok-check
language: go
severity: warning
message: Map lookup without an ok check. A missing key returns the zero value, which can hide bugs.
note: Always use the v, ok := m[key] pattern to check key presence, and write
  the handling for ok == false explicitly.
rule:
  pattern: $VALUE = $MAP[$KEY]

# Hardcoded-credential detection (CWE-798).
#
# Detects string literals that begin with a well-known credential prefix
# (OpenAI sk-, AWS access-key AKIA, GitHub token ghp_, Slack token xox*-,
# Google API key AIza). The prefix + minimum-length anchoring keeps the match
# precise: a benign string that merely contains these characters mid-value is
# not flagged, and neither is a value loaded from an environment variable or a
# secret manager.
#
# Every language below carries the identical pattern-family with equal
# opportunity. Languages not yet listed are equal-priority future additions.
---
id: sec-hardcoded-credential
language: go
severity: error
message: "A credential appears to be hardcoded in source. Load it from an environment variable or a secret manager instead."
note: "A hardcoded credential leaks through the source repository, its history, and every clone. Read the value from os.Getenv or a secret manager at runtime."
metadata:
  owasp: "A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures"
  cwe: "CWE-798"
  anchor: |
    probe: printf 'bearer := "sk-proj-demo"\n' > f.go; sg scan --config sgconfig.yml f.go
    -> error[sec-hardcoded-credential]: A credential appears to be hardcoded in source.
rule:
  kind: interpreted_string_literal
  regex: "^\"(sk-|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[0-9A-Za-z]{36}|xox[baprs]-|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35})"
---
id: sec-hardcoded-credential
language: python
severity: error
message: "A credential appears to be hardcoded in source. Load it from an environment variable or a secret manager instead."
note: "A hardcoded credential leaks through the source repository, its history, and every clone. Read the value from os.environ or a secret manager at runtime."
metadata:
  owasp: "A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures"
  cwe: "CWE-798"
  anchor: |
    probe: printf 'bearer = "sk-proj-demo"\n' > f.py; sg scan --config sgconfig.yml f.py
    -> error[sec-hardcoded-credential]: A credential appears to be hardcoded in source.
rule:
  kind: string
  regex: "^[\"'](sk-|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[0-9A-Za-z]{36}|xox[baprs]-|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35})"
---
id: sec-hardcoded-credential
language: javascript
severity: error
message: "A credential appears to be hardcoded in source. Load it from an environment variable or a secret manager instead."
note: "A hardcoded credential leaks through the source repository, its history, and every clone. Read the value from process.env or a secret manager at runtime."
metadata:
  owasp: "A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures"
  cwe: "CWE-798"
  anchor: |
    probe: printf 'const bearer = "sk-proj-demo";\n' > f.js; sg scan --config sgconfig.yml f.js
    -> error[sec-hardcoded-credential]: A credential appears to be hardcoded in source.
rule:
  kind: string
  regex: "^[\"'](sk-|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[0-9A-Za-z]{36}|xox[baprs]-|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35})"
---
id: sec-hardcoded-credential
language: typescript
severity: error
message: "A credential appears to be hardcoded in source. Load it from an environment variable or a secret manager instead."
note: "A hardcoded credential leaks through the source repository, its history, and every clone. Read the value from process.env or a secret manager at runtime."
metadata:
  owasp: "A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures"
  cwe: "CWE-798"
  anchor: |
    probe: printf 'const bearer: string = "sk-proj-demo";\n' > f.ts; sg scan --config sgconfig.yml f.ts
    -> error[sec-hardcoded-credential]: A credential appears to be hardcoded in source.
rule:
  kind: string
  regex: "^[\"'](sk-|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[0-9A-Za-z]{36}|xox[baprs]-|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35})"

# Weak-cryptography detection (CWE-327).
#
# Detects use of the MD5 hash constructor, which is unsuitable for any security
# purpose (it is vulnerable to collision attacks). This is deliberately narrow:
# it flags the constructor call, not incidental references, so a clean sample
# using a strong hash produces zero findings.
#
# Languages not yet listed are equal-priority future additions.
---
id: sec-weak-hash-md5
language: go
severity: error
message: "MD5 is unsuitable for security use. Use crypto/sha256 or stronger, or bcrypt/argon2 for password hashing."
note: "MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and must not be used for integrity or authentication. Use SHA-256/SHA-512 for hashing, or a password-hashing function such as bcrypt or argon2 for passwords."
metadata:
  owasp: "A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures"
  cwe: "CWE-327"
  anchor: >-
    cite: Go standard library, crypto/md5 - func New() hash.Hash, the MD5
    constructor this pattern matches.
rule:
  pattern: md5.New()

# Command-injection detection (CWE-78).
#
# Detects the canonical shell-execution constructs where an unvalidated value
# can reach a shell interpreter: Go's exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...), Python's
# subprocess shell=True / os.system, and Node's child_process.exec. Each rule
# is scoped to the specific dangerous call so a benign, argument-list-based
# invocation (which does not spawn a shell) is not flagged.
#
# Every language below carries the identical pattern-family with equal
# opportunity. Languages not yet listed are equal-priority future additions.
---
id: sec-command-injection-shell
language: go
severity: error
message: "A shell command is built with exec.Command(\"sh\", \"-c\", ...). If any argument derives from external input, this is a command-injection risk."
note: "Passing a value to sh -c lets shell metacharacters execute. Prefer exec.Command with an explicit argument list and no shell, and validate any external input against an allowlist."
metadata:
  owasp: "A03:2021 - Injection"
  cwe: "CWE-78"
  anchor: >-
    cite: Go standard library, os/exec - func Command(name string, arg ...string)
    *Cmd; invoking it with "sh" "-c" routes the third argument through a shell.
rule:
  pattern: exec.Command("sh", "-c", $CMD)
---
id: sec-command-injection-shell
language: python
severity: error
message: "A shell command is executed with shell=True or os.system. If any argument derives from external input, this is a command-injection risk."
note: "shell=True and os.system route the command through a shell, so metacharacters execute. Pass an argument list without shell=True and validate any external input against an allowlist."
metadata:
  owasp: "A03:2021 - Injection"
  cwe: "CWE-78"
  anchor: >-
    cite: Python standard library - os.system(command) and the subprocess
    Popen/run/call shell=True argument, both of which execute through a shell.
rule:
  any:
    - pattern: subprocess.call($CMD, shell=True)
    - pattern: subprocess.run($CMD, shell=True)
    - pattern: subprocess.Popen($CMD, shell=True)
    - pattern: os.system($CMD)
---
id: sec-command-injection-exec
language: javascript
severity: error
message: "A shell command is executed with child_process.exec. If any argument derives from external input, this is a command-injection risk."
note: "child_process.exec runs the command through a shell, so metacharacters execute. Prefer child_process.execFile or spawn with an explicit argument list, and validate any external input against an allowlist."
metadata:
  owasp: "A03:2021 - Injection"
  cwe: "CWE-78"
  anchor: >-
    cite: Node.js child_process - child_process.exec(command[, options][,
    callback]) spawns a shell and executes the command within it.
rule:
  any:
    - pattern: child_process.exec($CMD)
    - pattern: cp.exec($CMD)
---
id: sec-command-injection-exec
language: typescript
severity: error
message: "A shell command is executed with child_process.exec. If any argument derives from external input, this is a command-injection risk."
note: "child_process.exec runs the command through a shell, so metacharacters execute. Prefer child_process.execFile or spawn with an explicit argument list, and validate any external input against an allowlist."
metadata:
  owasp: "A03:2021 - Injection"
  cwe: "CWE-78"
  anchor: >-
    cite: Node.js child_process - child_process.exec(command[, options][,
    callback]) spawns a shell and executes the command within it.
rule:
  any:
    - pattern: child_process.exec($CMD)
    - pattern: cp.exec($CMD)

---
id: sec-hardcoded-api-key
language: go
severity: error
message: API key hardcoded in source. Use an environment variable or a secrets management service.
note: Hardcoded secret values leak through the source repository. Use
  os.Getenv() or a vault.
# Expressed as a const-spec node carrying an anchored sk- literal rather than
# a plain pattern: the original pattern form silently matched nothing under
# ast-grep 0.40.x, while this form fires on the same construct.
rule:
  kind: const_spec
  regex: '"sk-'
metadata:
  owasp: A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
  cwe: CWE-798
  anchor: |
    probe: printf 'const openAiKey = "sk-live-alpha"\n' > f.go; sg scan
    --config sgconfig.yml f.go -> error[sec-hardcoded-api-key]: API key hardcoded
    in source.
---
id: sec-hardcoded-jwt-signing-key
language: go
severity: error
message: JWT signing key hardcoded as a literal byte slice. Load it from an environment variable.
note: A JWT signing key in code allows token forgery. Load a random key of at
  least 256 bits from the environment.
# Expressed as an anchored call-node regex (any receiver, literal []byte
# argument) for the same engine-behavior reason as its sibling above.
rule:
  kind: call_expression
  regex: '\.SignedString\(\[\]byte\("'
metadata:
  owasp: A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
  cwe: CWE-321
  anchor: >-
    cite: golang-jwt/jwt - func (t *Token) SignedString(key interface{}) (string,
    error), the signing call whose []byte literal argument this pattern matches.

---
id: sec-template-injection-html
language: go
severity: error
message: Marking user input as trusted HTML via html/template.HTML() enables XSS.
note: The template.HTML() conversion bypasses escaping. Never use it on user
  input; where unavoidable, sanitize with a library such as bluemonday.
# Expressed as a call node with an anchored literal prefix rather than a plain
# pattern: ast-grep 0.40.x silently matches nothing for this dotted-call shape,
# while the call_expression + regex form fires precisely (same family form as
# the credential rules).
rule:
  kind: call_expression
  regex: '^template\.HTML\('
metadata:
  owasp: A03:2021 - Injection
  cwe: CWE-79
  anchor: >-
    cite: Go standard library, html/template - type HTML string, documented as
    content that is emitted without escaping.
---
id: sec-log-injection-unsanitized
language: go
severity: warning
message: External input written to logs verbatim. Log injection can corrupt the logs.
note: Escape user input before logging, e.g. with fmt.Sprintf(%q) or
  strconv.Quote(). Embedded newlines break log parsing.
rule:
  pattern: log.Printf($FORMAT, $$$ARGS)
metadata:
  owasp: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
  cwe: CWE-117
  anchor: >-
    cite: Go standard library, log - func Printf(format string, v ...any), the
    formatted-write call this pattern matches.
---
id: sec-csrf-no-token-check
language: go
severity: warning
message: POST handler without CSRF token verification. Potentially vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
note: Apply gorilla/csrf or an equivalent middleware to every state-changing
  POST/PUT/DELETE endpoint.
rule:
  pattern: "func $HANDLER(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n  $$$BODY\n}\n"
metadata:
  owasp: A01:2021 - Broken Access Control
  cwe: CWE-352
  anchor: >-
    cite: Go standard library, net/http - type HandlerFunc func(ResponseWriter,
    *Request), the handler signature this pattern matches.

# ast-grep project configuration for the MoAI curated ruleset.
#
# ruleDirs lists ONLY directories that ship at least one production-vetted rule.
# Every rule under these directories has been verified against a positive fixture
# (it matches its intended construct) and a negative fixture (a clean sample
# produces zero findings).
#
# Language coverage is intentionally partial and treated with equal opportunity:
# a language that does not yet appear in a rule directory is an equal-priority
# future addition, never an unsupported one. New languages are added by shipping
# a vetted rule for that language under the relevant directory.
ruleDirs:
  - go
  - security

# Rule tests live OUTSIDE this distributed tree, repo-side, so the deliberate
# dangerous constructs in their fixtures never ship to user projects and never
# land inside the tree this ruleset scans. The relative path resolves from the
# directory holding this file and traverses upward out of it; where that path
# is absent (the state of every deployed project), `ast-grep scan` ignores the
# missing test root and scans normally.
testConfigs:
  - testDir: ../../../../../../internal/astgrep/testdata/rule-tests

# Default Evaluator Profile

Standard skeptical evaluation for general-purpose code review.

## Evaluation Dimensions

| Dimension | Weight | Pass Threshold |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| Functionality | 40% | All acceptance criteria PASS |
| Security | 25% | No Critical/High findings |
| Craft | 20% | Coverage >= 85% |
| Consistency | 15% | No major pattern violations |

## Must-Pass Criteria

- Functionality: All SPEC acceptance criteria must be met (no partial credit)
- Security: No Critical or High severity findings (FAIL overrides overall score)

## Hard Thresholds

- Security FAIL = Overall FAIL (regardless of other scores)
- Coverage below 85% = Craft FAIL

## Evaluation Rules

- Require concrete evidence for every PASS verdict
- Mark unverifiable criteria as UNVERIFIED, not PASS
- Report all findings with file:line references
- Provide actionable fix recommendations for every FAIL

## Finding-Stage Reporting (coverage before filtering)

At the finding stage, report every issue you find, including ones you are uncertain about or consider low-severity, each with a confidence level and an estimated severity. Do not filter for importance or confidence while finding — the verdict stage (must-pass thresholds + harmonic scoring) does the filtering downstream. The goal at this stage is coverage: surfacing a finding that later gets filtered out is preferable to silently dropping a real bug.

## Scoring Rubric

### Functionality (40%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | All acceptance criteria pass with edge cases verified |
| 0.75 | All primary acceptance criteria pass; minor edge cases missing |
| 0.50 | Core functionality works; 1-2 acceptance criteria fail or are unverified |
| 0.25 | Basic skeleton present but multiple acceptance criteria fail |

### Security (25%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | No findings of any severity; OWASP Top 10 checked |
| 0.75 | No Critical/High findings; Medium findings documented with mitigations |
| 0.50 | No Critical findings; High findings present but contained |
| 0.25 | Critical or multiple High findings present (triggers overall FAIL) |

### Craft (20%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | Coverage >= 85%, clean code, no duplication, clear naming |
| 0.75 | Coverage >= 80%, minor style issues, acceptable naming |
| 0.50 | Coverage >= 70%, some duplication or unclear naming |
| 0.25 | Coverage < 70% or significant code quality issues |

### Consistency (15%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | Fully consistent with project conventions and existing patterns |
| 0.75 | Minor deviations from conventions; no structural inconsistencies |
| 0.50 | Some pattern violations; deviations are localized |
| 0.25 | Significant inconsistencies with existing codebase patterns |

## D7/D8 Plan-Phase Dimensions

The following two dimensions are evaluated by plan-auditor during plan-phase
audit, not by sync-auditor during run-phase. They are listed here for
cross-reference visibility — the weights apply ONLY to plan-auditor's PASS/FAIL
decision and do NOT contribute to sync-auditor's 4-dimension overall score
(Functionality/Security/Craft/Consistency above).

| Plan-Auditor Dimension | Weight in Plan Verdict | Pass Threshold |
|------------------------|-----------------------:|----------------|
| D7 Cross-SPEC Reconciliation | 50% | No BLOCKING finding |
| D8 Cross-Platform Discipline | 50% | No BLOCKING finding |

Both dimensions use binary BLOCKING/PASS semantics — any single BLOCKING
finding fails plan-auditor's overall verdict regardless of other scores.

See `.claude/agents/moai/plan-auditor.md` Group 7 + Group 8 for the full
verification verbs and rubric.

# Strict Evaluator Profile

Enhanced security and reliability evaluation for critical systems (auth, payment, migration).

## Evaluation Dimensions

| Dimension | Weight | Pass Threshold |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| Functionality | 35% | All acceptance criteria PASS + edge cases verified |
| Security | 35% | Full OWASP Top 10 audit, no findings of any severity |
| Craft | 20% | Coverage >= 90%, mutation testing score >= 80% |
| Consistency | 10% | Strict pattern adherence |

## Must-Pass Criteria

- All four dimensions must individually score >= 80% (0.80) to pass
- Security: Zero findings at any severity level (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info)
- Functionality: All edge cases must be explicitly tested and verified
- No UNVERIFIED criteria allowed — everything must be demonstrated

## Hard Thresholds

- Security ANY finding = Overall FAIL (even Low/Info severity)
- Coverage below 90% = Craft FAIL
- Any UNVERIFIED criterion = Overall FAIL (must verify everything)
- Any dimension below 0.80 = Overall FAIL

## Additional Checks

- Input validation on all external boundaries
- Error handling for all failure paths
- No hardcoded credentials or secrets
- Parameterized queries for all database access
- Rate limiting on authentication endpoints

## Scoring Rubric

### Functionality (35%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | All acceptance criteria pass; all edge cases verified with tests; no UNVERIFIED items |
| 0.75 | All primary criteria pass; edge cases documented but not all tested (triggers FAIL in strict) |
| 0.50 | Core functionality verified; some edge cases missing (FAIL) |
| 0.25 | Multiple criteria unverified or failing (FAIL) |

### Security (35%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | Zero findings at any severity; full OWASP Top 10 audit passed; threat model reviewed |
| 0.75 | No Critical/High; Medium findings present with mitigations (triggers FAIL in strict) |
| 0.50 | No Critical; High or Medium findings present (FAIL) |
| 0.25 | Critical findings present (FAIL) |

### Craft (20%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | Coverage >= 90%, mutation score >= 80%, zero linting warnings, excellent naming |
| 0.75 | Coverage >= 85%, mutation score >= 70%, minor issues (triggers FAIL in strict) |
| 0.50 | Coverage >= 80%, mutation score below 70% (FAIL) |
| 0.25 | Coverage below 80% or no mutation testing (FAIL) |

### Consistency (10%)

| Score | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 1.00 | All code strictly follows established project patterns and conventions |
| 0.75 | Minor deviations with documented rationale (triggers FAIL in strict) |
| 0.50 | Multiple deviations from conventions (FAIL) |
| 0.25 | Significant structural inconsistencies (FAIL) |

# Pre-commit quality gate configuration.
#
# The gate detects the project language from marker files (go.mod, package.json,
# pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, ...) and runs the matching vet/lint/test toolchain
# before git commit. Tools that are not installed are skipped gracefully.
#
# The ast_grep_gate sub-section controls the ast-grep domain-rule scan step.
# It is ON by default in advisory mode (findings reported, commits never
# blocked); blocking is opt-in via block_on_error/warn_only_mode below. When
# the `sg` CLI is absent, the scan is skipped gracefully with a notice.
# Known limitation: the PreToolUse hook budget is 5s while the scan timeout is
# 30s; in advisory mode a timeout only loses the advisory output.
gate:
  enabled: true
  skip_tests: false
  # Disable individual steps by step name (e.g. "mypy", "dotnet format",
  # "pytest"). Note the inverted convention: an entry whose value is FALSE
  # skips that step. Omit the section entirely to run every detected step.
  disabled_steps: {}
  timeouts:
    vet: 30
    lint: 60
    test: 120
    # A type-check over a large monorepo routinely outlasts the test budget,
    # so it gets its own.
    typecheck: 300
    # How long a starting `moai gate` run waits for the gate-run lock — the
    # advisory lock that serializes concurrent manual gate runs in one
    # project — before degrading to an unserialized run. On expiry the run
    # proceeds and reports that it did; the lock never fails the gate.
    lock_wait: 30
  # The typecheck axis runs between vet and lint, so a type error surfaces
  # before the slower style pass and a project whose linter config is absent
  # still gets a correctness gate.
  #
  # Node resolves in three tiers: `command` below (any language), then
  # package.json scripts.typecheck, then `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit` when a
  # tsconfig.json is present. A solution-style tsconfig (files: [] plus
  # references) is refused rather than run — it type-checks nothing and would
  # pass vacuously.
  #
  # Every outcome is reported. A skip is not a failure, but it is never
  # silent: a language with no default prints how to supply one.
  typecheck:
    enabled: true
    # Overrides the language default and enables the axis for ANY language,
    # e.g. "mypy --strict ." or "npm run typecheck".
    #
    # Split on whitespace and executed directly, so shell metacharacters are
    # NOT interpreted — put a pipeline or a redirect in a script and name the
    # script here.
    command: ""
  # Pre-commit context: the git pre-commit hook's `moai gate` invocation.
  # The project-wide heavy steps (vet / lint / test / typecheck) are OFF there
  # by default, so one pre-existing failure unrelated to your staged change
  # cannot block every commit; the hook still runs the fast staged-files
  # subset (gofmt + go vet) on every commit. Set enabled: true to opt in and
  # block commits on project-wide failures — e.g. via `moai web`, Gate panel.
  # A standalone `moai gate` run ignores this key and keeps following the
  # `enabled` key above.
  pre_commit:
    enabled: false
  ast_grep_gate:
    enabled: true
    # Where this project's ast-grep rules live. This is the single source of
    # truth: the code carries no fallback default, and `moai ast-grep` /
    # `moai ast-edit` resolve their --rules-dir from this key when the flag
    # is omitted. The value below is where `moai init`/`moai update` deploy
    # the bundled ruleset; keep it in sync if you move the rules.
    rules_dir: ".moai/config/astgrep-rules"
    block_on_error: true
    warn_only_mode: false
  # The graph-freshness step checks the staleness of the project's graph
  # layers (codemaps docs, the @MX index, the edges artifact) before commit
  # and reports a per-layer verdict. Advisory by default — pre-commit is the
  # wrong place to force a docs regeneration — with blocking opt-in below.
  # The verdict is always emitted; a disabled step emits an explicit skip
  # notice, never silence. Run `moai graph check` standalone for the full
  # numeric report and exit codes.
  graph_freshness:
    enabled: true
    blocking: false
    # Red line for the codemaps layer: at or above this many described-source
    # files changed since the docs' stamped generation commit, the layer is
    # stale. Calibrate to your repository's docs-regeneration cadence.
    codemaps_changed_files: 40
    # Red line for the @MX index: at or above this many scanned files changed
    # content since the last scan, the index is stale (it is cheap to rescan).
    mx_index_changed_files: 1
    # Query-time refresh cost budget in milliseconds. A refresh that exceeds
    # it warns and still answers; it never blocks.
    update_budget_ms: 2000

# Harness Depth Configuration
# Defines quality pipeline depth levels and auto-detection thresholds.
# The system automatically selects the appropriate level based on SPEC complexity.
harness:
  # Default evaluator profile (used when SPEC has no evaluator_profile field)
  default_profile: "default"
  # @MX:NOTE: FROZEN at per_iteration per design-constitution §11.4.1; loader enforces via HRN_EVAL_MEMORY_FROZEN
  evaluator:
    memory_scope: per_iteration
  # Execution mode defaults
  mode_defaults:
    solo: auto # Sub-agent mode: auto-detect level
    team: auto # Team mode: auto-detect level
    cg: thorough # CG mode: always thorough (natural Generator-Evaluator split)
  # Automatic level detection (Complexity Estimator)
  auto_detection:
    enabled: true
    rules:
      minimal:
        conditions:
          - "file_count <= 3 AND single_domain"
          - "spec_type in [bugfix, docs, config]"
      standard:
        conditions:
          - "file_count > 3 OR multi_domain"
          - "spec_type in [feature, refactor]"
      thorough:
        conditions:
          - "security_keywords OR payment_keywords present"
          - "spec_priority == critical"
          - "domain in [auth, payment, migration, public_api]"
  # Failure-triggered escalation
  escalation:
    enabled: true
    triggers:
      - quality_gate_fail # Phase 2.5 FAIL -> escalate one level
      - review_critical # Phase 2.8 CRITICAL -> escalate to thorough
      - test_coverage_low # Coverage < 70% -> escalate to standard+
    max_escalations: 2
  # Effort level mapping
  # Maps harness depth to CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL for Opus 4.7 adaptive thinking.
  # Deeper harness = more extended reasoning budget for evaluator and planner agents.
  effort_mapping:
    minimal: "low" # Fast iteration: no extended reasoning
    standard: "medium" # Balanced quality: moderate reasoning budget
    thorough: "high" # Critical features: maximum reasoning budget
  # [HARD] Global plan_audit override — prevents incident recurrence
  #
  # In a prior incident, 30 SPECs were generated without going through the plan-auditor
  # gate because: (a) /moai project scope creep bypassed /moai plan entirely, and
  # (b) the minimal level had plan_audit.enabled: false. Result: 386 cross-SPEC
  # defects (100% FAIL rate) that required emergency remediation.
  #
  # This global override enforces plan_audit on ALL levels regardless of
  # auto_detection output. The per-level plan_audit.enabled below is now
  # treated as a hint for max_iterations only — the gate itself is always on.
  plan_audit_global:
    always_enabled: true # [HARD] Cannot be disabled by auto_detection
    enforce_gate_on_spec_creation: true # [HARD] Blocks SPEC creation outside /moai plan
    rationale: "prevent scope-creep SPEC generation"
  # Per-Tier plan-auditor retry ceiling SSOT.
  # The plan-auditor agent body consults the Tier-resolved value from this map
  # INSTEAD of a hard-coded `max_iterations: 3` literal; the literal is a
  # consumer-side fallback, NOT the SSOT. Backward compat: when `tier:` is
  # absent from a SPEC's frontmatter, the Tier L value (3) is used.
  plan_audit_tier_ceilings:
    S: 1 # Tier S (≤300 LOC, <5 files): single-pass audit, no iteration 2+
    M: 2 # Tier M (300-1000 LOC, 5-15 files): up to two spawns
    L: 3 # Tier L (>1000 LOC or constitutional): up to three spawns (legacy behavior)
  # Level definitions
  levels:
    minimal:
      description: "Fast iteration for simple changes"
      skip_phases: [0, 0.5, 2.0, 2.5, 2.75, 2.8a, 2.9, 2.10]
      evaluator: false
      sprint_contract: false
      plan_audit:
        # NOTE: plan_audit_global.always_enabled overrides this to true.
        # This field now controls max_iterations defaults only.
        enabled: true
        max_iterations: 1 # Minimal level: single-pass audit (fast)
        require_must_pass: false # Relaxed for minimal: warn but do not block
    standard:
      description: "Balanced quality for most development"
      skip_phases: []
      evaluator: true
      evaluator_mode: "final-pass"
      sprint_contract: false
      plan_audit:
        enabled: true
        max_iterations: 3
        require_must_pass: true
    thorough:
      description: "Maximum quality for critical features"
      skip_phases: []
      evaluator: true
      evaluator_mode: "per-sprint"
      evaluator_profile: "strict"
      sprint_contract: true
      playwright_testing: true
      plan_audit:
        enabled: true
        max_iterations: 3
        require_must_pass: true
        cross_validate_with_evaluator_active: true
  # Model Upgrade Review Process
  # When Claude model is upgraded, review harness components for simplification.
  # Reference: Anthropic "Harness Design for Long-Running Apps" (2025)
  # DORMANT-in-practice: the model_upgrade_review consumer (emitModelUpgradeReminder)
  # exists, but its CLAUDE_MODEL_PREVIOUS / CLAUDE_MODEL trigger env vars have no
  # setter anywhere — the review never fires. Preserved for forward compatibility.
  model_upgrade_review:
    enabled: true
    # Checklist items to evaluate after model upgrade
    checklist:
      - id: sprint_necessity
        question: "Are per-sprint evaluations still needed, or can the model handle end-to-run evaluation?"
        action: "If model handles longer coherent work, switch evaluator_mode from per-sprint to final-pass"
        affects: "levels.thorough.evaluator_mode"
      - id: context_reset_necessity
        question: "Does the model still exhibit context anxiety near window limits?"
        action: "If no context anxiety, reduce auto_clear frequency or increase token_threshold"
        affects: "workflow.yaml auto_clear.token_threshold"
      - id: evaluator_skepticism
        question: "Has model self-evaluation improved enough to reduce evaluator iterations?"
        action: "If self-evaluation is reliable, consider reducing gan_loop.max_iterations"
        affects: "config.yaml gan_loop.max_iterations"
      - id: parallel_safety
        question: "Can the model safely coordinate more parallel agents without conflicts?"
        action: "If coordination improved, consider increasing parallel agent limits"
        affects: "workflow.yaml team settings"
      - id: guardrail_necessity
        question: "Are any minimal-level skip_phases still necessary for the upgraded model?"
        action: "Review each skipped phase — remove skip if model can handle the phase efficiently"
        affects: "levels.minimal.skip_phases"
      - id: harness_level_thresholds
        question: "Should auto_detection thresholds be adjusted for improved model capabilities?"
        action: "If model handles complexity better, raise minimal threshold (more tasks qualify as minimal)"
        affects: "auto_detection.rules"
    # When to trigger review
    trigger:
      on_model_change: true # Auto-trigger when model version changes
      manual_command: "moai review --harness" # Manual trigger command
      review_interval_days: 90 # Periodic review even without model change
    # Review output
    output:
      report_path: ".moai/reports/harness-review.md"
      require_approval: true # Human must approve harness changes
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Harness Learning Subsystem Configuration
# Learning behavior parameters, defined under the learning: key.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
learning:
  # Whether the observer + learner are enabled (default true).
  # Setting false makes RecordEvent and AggregatePatterns both no-ops.
  enabled: true
  # Whether to apply automatically upon reaching Tier 4 (default false).
  # When false, user approval via AskUserQuestion is required.
  # auto_apply default value MUST be false.
  auto_apply: false
  # Tier promotion thresholds [Observation, Heuristic, Rule, AutoUpdate].
  # Default [1, 3, 5, 10] — changing this alters ClassifyTier behavior.
  tier_thresholds: [1, 3, 5, 10]
  # Automatic update rate limit.
  rate_limit:
    max_per_week: 3 # Maximum allowed updates within a 7-day sliding window
    cooldown_hours: 24 # Minimum wait time between updates (hours)
  # Retention period for usage-log.jsonl (days).
  log_retention_days: 90

# LSP Configuration for MoAI-ADK
#
# ================================================================
# Language Neutrality Policy (per .claude/rules/moai/development/coding-standards.md § Language Policy)
# ================================================================
# This is a TEMPLATE file deployed to end-user projects via
# `moai init`. MoAI-ADK supports 16 programming languages, and
# this file MUST treat all of them as equal first-class citizens.
#
# The author of MoAI-ADK writes Go; users of MoAI-ADK may write
# ANY of the 16 supported languages. Do NOT encode the author's
# language preference into this template.
#
# Supported languages (all 16 equal, alphabetical):
#   cpp, csharp, elixir, flutter, go, java, javascript, kotlin,
#   php, python, r, ruby, rust, scala, swift, typescript
#
# Note: "flutter" is the canonical name for the Dart/Flutter ecosystem,
# matching .claude/skills/moai/workflows/sync.md Phase 0.6.1 and
# .claude/rules/moai/languages/flutter.md.
# ================================================================
#
# Architecture: MoAI-ADK is an LSP CLIENT + AGGREGATOR
#   - Spawns existing language server binaries per user's project
#   - Aggregates diagnostics from all active servers
#   - Does NOT reimplement per-language analyzers
#
# Lazy activation: a language server is only started when a file
# matching its project_markers is encountered. Users working on a
# single-language project only pay the cost of that one server.
#
# Fallback: ast-grep / Tree-sitter provides AST analysis for all
# 16 languages via .moai/config/astgrep-rules/. When no LSP
# binary is available, ast-grep continues to provide quality gates.
#
# Research sources (comparative audit):
#   - sst/opencode: lazy init, 20+ languages, stdio
#   - charmbracelet/crush: manager-coordinator + powernap
#   - ktnyt/cclsp: robust position resolution for AI agents
#   - plandex-ai/plandex & aider: Tree-sitter fallback pattern

lsp:
  # Master switch. Flip to true once the runtime LSP client lands
  # (powernap-based, multi-language design).
  enabled: false

  # Client implementation selector.
  # Accepted values:
  #   gopls_bridge  — legacy Go-only bridge. Default.
  #   powernap_core — multi-language foundation (charmbracelet/powernap).
  # Empty defaults to "gopls_bridge". Read by the internal LSP config loader.
  client_impl: gopls_bridge

  # ---------------- 16 Language Server Matrix ----------------
  # All 16 MoAI-supported languages, listed alphabetically, with
  # identical schema. No language receives PRIMARY / SECONDARY /
  # DEFERRED classification; the user's project_markers decide
  # which servers actually spawn at runtime.
  #
  # Schema per entry:
  #   command              : Primary server executable
  #   fallback_binaries    : Alternative servers if primary missing
  #   args                 : Command-line arguments
  #   init_options         : LSP initializationOptions for the server
  #   project_markers      : Files that identify this language
  #                          (LSP client spawns server only when a
  #                          marker exists in the user's project)
  #   install_hint         : Human-readable install command
  #   license_concern      : "open" | "commercial" (user awareness)
  servers:

    cpp:
      command: clangd
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "CMakeLists.txt"
        - "compile_commands.json"
        - "Makefile"
      install_hint: "Install clangd from an LLVM distribution (brew install llvm | apt install clangd | winget install LLVM.LLVM)"
      file_extensions:
        - ".cpp"
        - ".cc"
        - ".cxx"
        - ".h"
        - ".hpp"
      license_concern: "open"

    csharp:
      command: omnisharp
      fallback_binaries:
        - "roslyn-ls"
      args:
        - "-lsp"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "*.csproj"
        - "*.sln"
        - "*.fsproj"
      install_hint: "Install OmniSharp or Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer"
      file_extensions:
        - ".cs"
      license_concern: "open"

    flutter:
      command: dart
      fallback_binaries: []
      args:
        - "language-server"
        - "--protocol=lsp"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "pubspec.yaml"
        - "pubspec.lock"
      install_hint: "Install Dart SDK or Flutter SDK (dart binary provides language server)"
      file_extensions:
        - ".dart"
      license_concern: "open"

    elixir:
      command: elixir-ls
      fallback_binaries:
        - "lexical"
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "mix.exs"
        - "mix.lock"
      install_hint: "Install elixir-ls from https://github.com/elixir-lsp/elixir-ls"
      file_extensions:
        - ".ex"
        - ".exs"
      license_concern: "open"

    go:
      command: gopls
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options:
        staticcheck: true
      project_markers:
        - "go.mod"
        - "go.sum"
      install_hint: "go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest"
      file_extensions:
        - ".go"
      license_concern: "open"

    java:
      command: jdtls
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "pom.xml"
        - "build.gradle"
        - "build.gradle.kts"
      install_hint: "Install Eclipse JDT Language Server (jdtls)"
      file_extensions:
        - ".java"
      license_concern: "open"

    javascript:
      command: typescript-language-server
      fallback_binaries: []
      args:
        - "--stdio"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "package.json"
        - "jsconfig.json"
      install_hint: "npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript"
      file_extensions:
        - ".js"
        - ".jsx"
        - ".mjs"
      license_concern: "open"

    kotlin:
      command: kotlin-language-server
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "build.gradle.kts"
        - "build.gradle"
        - "settings.gradle.kts"
      install_hint: "Install from https://github.com/fwcd/kotlin-language-server"
      file_extensions:
        - ".kt"
        - ".kts"
      license_concern: "open"

    php:
      command: phpactor
      fallback_binaries:
        - "intelephense"
      args:
        - "language-server"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "composer.json"
        - "composer.lock"
      install_hint: "Install phpactor from https://phpactor.readthedocs.io/"
      file_extensions:
        - ".php"
      license_concern: "open"

    python:
      command: pylsp
      fallback_binaries:
        - "pyright-langserver"
        - "basedpyright-langserver"
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "pyproject.toml"
        - "setup.py"
        - "requirements.txt"
        - "Pipfile"
      install_hint: "pip install python-lsp-server"
      file_extensions:
        - ".py"
      license_concern: "open"

    r:
      command: R
      fallback_binaries: []
      args:
        - "--slave"
        - "-e"
        - "languageserver::run()"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "DESCRIPTION"
        - ".Rproj"
        - "renv.lock"
      install_hint: "install.packages('languageserver') in R"
      file_extensions:
        - ".R"
        - ".r"
      license_concern: "open"

    ruby:
      command: ruby-lsp
      fallback_binaries:
        - "solargraph"
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "Gemfile"
        - ".ruby-version"
        - "Rakefile"
      install_hint: "gem install ruby-lsp"
      file_extensions:
        - ".rb"
      license_concern: "open"

    rust:
      command: rust-analyzer
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options:
        checkOnSave:
          command: "clippy"
      project_markers:
        - "Cargo.toml"
        - "Cargo.lock"
      install_hint: "rustup component add rust-analyzer"
      file_extensions:
        - ".rs"
      license_concern: "open"

    scala:
      command: metals
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "build.sbt"
        - "build.sc"
      install_hint: "Install metals from https://scalameta.org/metals/"
      file_extensions:
        - ".scala"
        - ".sc"
      license_concern: "open"

    swift:
      command: sourcekit-lsp
      fallback_binaries: []
      args: []
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "Package.swift"
        - "*.xcodeproj"
        - "*.xcworkspace"
      install_hint: "Install the Swift toolchain — it ships sourcekit-lsp (macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools | Linux/Windows: swift.org/install)"
      file_extensions:
        - ".swift"
      license_concern: "open"

    typescript:
      command: typescript-language-server
      fallback_binaries: []
      args:
        - "--stdio"
      init_options: {}
      project_markers:
        - "tsconfig.json"
        - "package.json"
      install_hint: "npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript"
      file_extensions:
        - ".ts"
        - ".tsx"
      license_concern: "open"

  # ---------------- ast-grep Delegation ----------------
  # ast-grep / Tree-sitter provides AST analysis for ALL 16 languages.
  # This is independent of LSP and serves as universal fallback /
  # supplement. No language is excluded.
  delegate_to_astgrep:
    enabled: true
    rules_dir: ".moai/config/astgrep-rules"
    languages:
      - cpp
      - csharp
      - elixir
      - flutter
      - go
      - java
      - javascript
      - kotlin
      - php
      - python
      - r
      - ruby
      - rust
      - scala
      - swift
      - typescript

  # ---------------- Aggregator Settings ----------------
  # Applies equally to all 16 language servers.
  # Tuned from opencode/crush production research.
  aggregator:
    # Per-file diagnostic cache time-to-live
    cache_ttl_seconds: 5

    # Maximum simultaneous language server queries
    max_parallel_servers: 16

    # Server startup timeout (first file of a language)
    server_startup_timeout_seconds: 30

    # Per-request timeout for LSP method calls
    request_timeout_seconds: 5

    # Graceful shutdown timeout
    shutdown_timeout_seconds: 5

    # Debounce window for diagnostic notifications
    diagnostics_debounce_ms: 150

    # Use LSP 3.17+ pull diagnostic model
    diagnostic_pull_enabled: true

  # ---------------- Discovery Policy ----------------
  # Graceful degradation: missing binaries warn, never error.
  # Applies equally to all 16 languages.
  discovery:
    # Actions when a language server binary is not found
    # Options: warn_and_skip | error | silent_skip
    on_missing: "warn_and_skip"

    # Print install_hint when a server is missing
    auto_install_suggest: true

    # Search order for binaries
    search_paths:
      - "PATH"
      - "node_modules/.bin"
      - ".venv/bin"
      - ".tools/bin"

    # Auto-detect project language via project_markers
    auto_detect_language: true

  # ---------------- Circuit Breaker ----------------
  # Stop trying a failing server after N consecutive failures.
  # Applies equally to all 16 languages.
  circuit_breaker:
    threshold: 3
    open_duration_seconds: 30

constitution:
  # Development methodology selection
  # Options: ddd (Domain-Driven Development), tdd (Test-Driven Development)
  development_mode: tdd
  # Default session effort level for Opus models supporting effort control.
  # Applied when no agent-specific effort override exists.
  # Valid values: "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"
  # "xhigh" and "max" are available on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 4.8, and Opus 4.7.
  session_effort_default: "xhigh"
  # Enable TRUST 5 quality framework enforcement
  enforce_quality: true
  # Target code coverage percentage (0-100)
  test_coverage_target: 85
  # DDD Mode Settings (ANALYZE-PRESERVE-IMPROVE)
  # Best for: Existing projects with minimal test coverage (< 10%)
  ddd_settings:
    # Require existing tests before modifications
    require_existing_tests: true
    # Create characterization tests to capture current behavior
    characterization_tests: true
    # Capture behavior snapshots for regression detection
    behavior_snapshots: true
    # Limit transformation size (small, medium, large)
    max_transformation_size: small
    # Always preserve behavior before improving
    preserve_before_improve: true
  # TDD Mode Settings (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
  # Best for: All development work, new projects, and projects with 10%+ test coverage (default)
  tdd_settings:
    # Enforce RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle
    red_green_refactor: true
    # Tests must be written before implementation
    test_first_required: true
    # Minimum coverage percentage per commit (0-100)
    min_coverage_per_commit: 80
    # Enable mutation testing (experimental)
    mutation_testing_enabled: false
  # Coverage exemption settings
  coverage_exemptions:
    # Allow coverage exemptions with justification
    enabled: false
    # Require written justification for exemptions
    require_justification: true
    # Maximum percentage of code that can be exempt (0-100)
    max_exempt_percentage: 5
  # Test quality requirements
  test_quality:
    # Tests should be specification-based (behavior, not implementation)
    specification_based: true
    # Tests must have meaningful assertions
    meaningful_assertions: true
    # Avoid coupling tests to implementation details
    avoid_implementation_coupling: true
    # Enable mutation testing (experimental)
    mutation_testing_enabled: false
  # LSP-based quality gates
  lsp_quality_gates:
    # Enable LSP quality validation
    enabled: true
    # Plan phase requirements
    plan:
      # Capture LSP baseline at phase start
      require_baseline: true
    # Run phase requirements
    run:
      # Maximum allowed errors (0 = zero tolerance)
      max_errors: 0
      # Maximum allowed type errors (0 = zero tolerance)
      max_type_errors: 0
      # Maximum allowed lint errors (0 = zero tolerance)
      max_lint_errors: 0
      # Allow regression from baseline (false = zero tolerance)
      allow_regression: false
    # Sync phase requirements
    sync:
      # Maximum allowed errors (0 = zero tolerance)
      max_errors: 0
      # Maximum allowed warnings
      max_warnings: 10
      # Require clean LSP state
      require_clean_lsp: true
    # LSP cache time-to-live in seconds
    cache_ttl_seconds: 5
    # LSP operation timeout in seconds
    timeout_seconds: 3
  # ast-grep quality gate (pattern-based static analysis)
  # Rules loaded from rules_dir at pre-commit time.
  # A planned upgrade will extend the rule set to additional multi-language + security rules.
  ast_grep_gate:
    # Enable ast-grep quality checks (reverts a prior silent disable)
    enabled: true
    # Directory containing YAML rule files (relative to project root)
    rules_dir: ".moai/config/astgrep-rules"
    # Block commits on error-severity matches
    block_on_error: true
    # Report matches as warnings only (do not block)
    warn_only_mode: false
  # Quality principles
  principles:
    # Simplicity principle
    simplicity:
      # Maximum parallel tasks to prevent complexity
      max_parallel_tasks: 10
  # LSP integration settings
  lsp_integration:
    # TRUST 5 framework integration with LSP
    trust5_integration:
      # Tested dimension checks
      tested:
        - unit_tests_pass
        - lsp_type_errors == 0
        - lsp_errors == 0
      # Readable dimension checks
      readable:
        - naming_conventions_followed
        - lsp_lint_errors == 0
      # Understandable dimension checks
      understandable:
        - documentation_complete
        - code_complexity_acceptable
        - lsp_warnings < threshold
      # Secured dimension checks
      secured:
        - security_scan_pass
        - lsp_security_warnings == 0
      # Trackable dimension checks
      trackable:
        - logs_structured
        - lsp_diagnostic_history_tracked
    # LSP diagnostic sources to monitor
    diagnostic_sources:
      - typecheck
      - lint
      - security
    # Regression detection thresholds
    regression_detection:
      # Error increase threshold (0 = zero tolerance)
      error_increase_threshold: 0
      # Warning increase threshold
      warning_increase_threshold: 10
      # Type error increase threshold (0 = zero tolerance)
      type_error_increase_threshold: 0
  # Memory Guard: System memory awareness for test execution (opt-in)
  # Enable to prevent OOM kills on memory-constrained environments (WSL2, CI, VMs)
  memory_guard:
    enabled: false
    emergency_threshold_mb: 2048
    adaptive_threshold_mb: 8192
    test_split_strategy: "module"
    coverage_separate: true
# Report generation settings
report_generation:
  # Enable quality report generation
  enabled: true
  # Automatically create reports after each phase
  auto_create: false
  # Warn user when quality issues detected
  warn_user: true
  # Default report detail level (Minimal, Summary, Detailed)
  user_choice: Minimal
# LSP state tracking
lsp_state_tracking:
  # Enable LSP state tracking across phases
  enabled: true
  # Phase points where LSP state is captured
  capture_points:
    - phase_start
    - post_transformation
    - pre_sync
  # Comparison settings
  comparison:
    # Baseline for comparison (phase_start, previous, custom)
    baseline: phase_start
    # Regression detection threshold (0 = zero tolerance)
    regression_threshold: 0
  # Logging settings
  logging:
    # Log LSP state changes
    log_lsp_state_changes: true
    # Log regression detection events
    log_regression_detection: true
    # Include LSP diagnostics in quality reports
    include_lsp_in_reports: true

# Security Hardening Configuration
# Extra patterns extend (never replace) DefaultSecurityPolicy hardcoded patterns.
# Uses SOLID O-Principle: extend via config without modifying core.
security:
  # Additional dangerous Bash command patterns (regex, case-insensitive).
  # These are APPENDED to the built-in deny patterns.
  extra_dangerous_bash_patterns:
    - 'curl\s+.*\|\s*(ba)?sh' # curl pipe to shell
    - 'wget\s+.*\|\s*(ba)?sh' # wget pipe to shell
    - 'chmod\s+777' # world-writable permissions
    - 'rm\s+-rf\s+/[^.]' # rm -rf targeting root paths
    - 'mkfs\.' # filesystem format commands
    - 'dd\s+if=.*of=/dev/' # raw disk write
  # Additional file deny patterns (regex, case-insensitive).
  extra_deny_patterns: []
  # Additional file ask patterns (regex, case-insensitive).
  extra_ask_patterns: []
  # Additional sensitive content patterns (regex, case-insensitive).
  extra_sensitive_content_patterns: []
  # Permission subsystem keys.
  permission:
    # When strict_mode=true, agent spawn in bypassPermissions mode is rejected.
    strict_mode: true
    # SrcBuiltin pre-allowlist patterns (defaults — actual patterns defined in stack.go PreAllowlist()).
    pre_allowlist: []
    # session_rules: session-scoped rules loaded at the SrcSession tier.
    session_rules: []
  # Sandbox Execution Layer configuration.
  sandbox:
    # When required=true, agents with sandbox: none are rejected without sandbox.justification.
    # Default: false (v3.0 — considered for true in v3.1+).
    required: false
    # network_allowlist: additive list of allowed network hosts added to the default 8.
    # Defaults: github.com, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, proxy.golang.org,
    #           crates.io, repo.maven.apache.org, rubygems.org, pub.dev
    network_allowlist: []
    # env_scrub_extra: additive (not replacement) env var names added to the default scrub list.
    # Defaults: AWS_* (prefix), GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY,
    #           NPM_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN
    env_scrub_extra: []
    # docker_image: default image to use with the docker backend.
    # Temporary value before EXT-004 migration framework is complete: alpine:latest.
    docker_image: "alpine:latest"
